newsitem.title: USA: Northeast Utilities to meet with NRC.
newsitem.headline: Northeast Utilities to meet with NRC.

text.p: Northeast Utilities said Tuesday it will explain to the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) the steps it is taking to correct problems that resulted in the shutdown of its four nuclear plants earlier this year.
Officials from Northeast Utilities (NU) will meet with NRC representatives at an enforcement conference on Wednesday and Thursday.

"This will be a difficult but necessary process for Northeast Utilities Nuclear -- it is a process we must go through to fix our nuclear program," Bruce Kenyon, president and chief executive officer of NU Nuclear, said in a statement.
"In order for us to move forward, we must bring these past issues to closure."
Kenyon said the enforcement conference gives NU a chance to show the NRC and the public that it understood what caused the problems and that it is taking steps to address them.
"The underlying nature of our problems is this -- leadership's pervasive tolerance of low standards," said Kenyon.
"We've changed the leadership and we will no longer tolerate low standards. What we are doing is fundamentally changing how NU Nuclear functions."
Kenyon was brought in from the highly regarded South Carolina Electric and Gas Company in September to help salvage NU's nuclear operation.

NU's Connecticut Yankee nuclear plant in Haddam Neck, Conn., has been shut down since July 22. The plant's board of directors is expected to make an announcement Wednesday on whether the 28-year-old plant will be closed permanently.
NU's three Millstone nuclear plants have been idled by safety problems since March.
An NRC spokesman said earlier that the NRC would not make any decisions at this week's enforcement conference.
